training set: The examples a network learns from. Its homework.
test set: Examples held back and never trained on, used once at the very end to measure what the network really learned.
validation set: A third pile of held-back examples, used for making choices during training (such as when to stop) so that the test set can stay unseen.
generalize: To do well on examples that were not in the training data. It is the whole point of learning a rule instead of memorizing answers.
label noise: Wrong answers hiding in the training data, like typos in an answer key.
early stopping: Ending training at the moment the score on held-back data is at its best, before the network starts memorizing.
weight decay: A training trick that shrinks every weight a tiny bit on each step, which discourages the extreme weights that memorizing needs.
dropout: A training trick that switches off a random handful of neurons on every step, so the network cannot rely on any single neuron to memorize an example.
